after_swap_cases.notes: Removing only the try/catch (lead comment, `try {`, the catch block), with the ten steps back at their old indentation and byte-identical to the pre-Step-6 lines, makes both cases FAIL. Without the catch the throw from toast.success reaches the open path's own catch: the picker's `accept` for the picked file, `acceptDropped` for the dropped one. Either way the toast says 'Punk.gp could not be opened. Something went wrong on our side, not with your file. Try again, or reload the page. (Error E105)'. E105 is still reported exactly once without the catch, by that same catch, so the `reported('E105')` wait passes either way; the toast-text assertion is what tells the two apart. The dropped case's last assertion, no 'could not be opened. Error E105.' announcement, was never reached without the catch, because the toast assertion fails first. Reasoned, not run: 'reports E105 once' is checked only when waitFor first sees one report. A catch that also rethrew would still be caught: the second report and the 'could not be opened' toast would follow in the same microtask chain, so the count would read 2 and the not.toHaveBeenCalledWith assertion would also fail. The catch was restored (cmp-identical to the saved with-catch file) and both cases passed again: 2 passed | 3 skipped.

problems.what: Low, diagnostic only. In three of the new PlayerShell cases, `waitFor(..., { timeout: 5000 })` equals Vitest's default testTimeout (web/vitest.config.ts sets none), so the test's own timeout fires first. In the fail-first run, two cases ('a dropped file that fails after the read reports E105 and announces it' and 'a dropped file whose open fails after the swap says it opened, not that it failed') therefore die with Vitest's timeout and never print what reported('E105') held. They still fail for the right reason, and in the final state every case passes in at most about 2.1 s.
